item.title: Attorney General's office says it is confident in its prosecutors after two murder trial defeats
item.description: The Attorney General's office said it has confidence in the professionalism and commitment of its prosecutors as criticism grows over two high-profile murder trials it has lost in two months. A jury cleared Lorin Scicluna of the racially motivated killing of Lassana Cisse on Sunday, shortly after Yorgen Fenech was acquitted over the murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia. The office declined to comment on the evidence or on the separate case against Francesco Fenech. Nationalist MP Mark Anthony Sammut called the three jury losses in two months unprecedented and accused Attorney General Victoria Buttigieg of having weakened the office.

Sources: Times of Malta, Newsbook

item.title: PN says Budget 2027 fails to address traffic and education challenges
item.description: Nationalist shadow ministers Ivan Castillo and Jerome Caruana Cilia criticised Budget 2027 at a press conference, saying it leaves traffic congestion and structural education problems unaddressed. Castillo said congestion costs an estimated €770 million a year, potentially rising to €917 million, and questioned how long the proposed rapid transit system will take to materialise. Caruana Cilia said the shortage of learning support educators persists, cited an EY estimate that 550 more teachers will be needed over the next decade, and referred to Malta's worst PISA results since the country began taking part in the international assessment.

item.title: Pregnant non-EU workers already in Malta to retain free childcare
item.description: Third-country nationals already living in Malta and expecting a child will continue to benefit from free childcare, according to sources. Transitional arrangements will also cover children of TCNs already registered for childcare but not yet attending. The clarification follows revised criteria being drawn up by Jobsplus after Budget 2027 measures withdrew free childcare for non-EU nationals without long-term residency.

item.title: Five arrested in St Paul's Bay drug raid, 150 sachets seized
item.description: Police arrested five people, including a 16-year-old girl, in a drug trafficking operation in St Paul's Bay. Four were arrested after a tip-off, including a 25-year-old man, two 20-year-old men and the girl; a 27-year-old woman was arrested the following day. Officers seized around 150 sachets of suspected heroin, cocaine and cannabis, about €5,000 in cash and several mobile phones. An inquiry was opened before Magistrate Renata Farrugia.

item.title: Outbound trips up 5% in third quarter, NSO says
item.description: Total outbound tourist trips in the third quarter of 2026 were estimated at 284,486, up 5.1% on the same quarter of 2025, with nights spent rising 1.3%. Estimated expenditure stood at €303.0 million, or €1,065 per capita. Trips to non-EU countries rose 11.5%, and Italy remained the most popular destination with a 38.9% share.

item.title: Driving Licence Surrender Scheme applicants to get approval letters in coming weeks
item.description: Transport Malta said decision letters on Driving Licence Surrender Scheme applications will be issued in the coming weeks, after the scheme went unmentioned in Finance Minister Clyde Caruana's Budget 2027 speech and was omitted from the financial estimates. Approved applicants will be asked to surrender their licence and receive the first of five €5,000 lump sums. Two applicants said they were never interviewed and that the scheme's dedicated page had been taken down.

item.title: Scicluna to be sentenced today after Cisse murder acquittal
item.description: Lorin Scicluna is due to be sentenced at 12.30pm on Wednesday after a jury cleared him of the 2019 murder of Lassana Cisse. He was found guilty only of grievously injuring May Malimi, who was hit by his car in February 2019, and of driving without a number plate. His co-accused Francesco Fenech is still charged over the murder and is to be tried separately.

item.title: Medical association threatens industrial action over training recruitment delays
item.description: The Medical Association of Malta said it will pursue industrial action if delays persist in the recruitment process for specialist medical and surgical training. The current call opened on 15 May 2026, and applicants are still awaiting confirmation of appointments. The association said the Public Service Commission rejected a proposal to expedite the process, and demanded a time-bound recruitment protocol and a formal review of the delays.

item.title: Clean-up begins at Manoel Island ahead of national park plans
item.description: Cleaning and maintenance works have begun at Manoel Island, Gżira, as the first step towards turning it into a national park open to the public. The works, carried out by the Cleansing and Maintenance Division with Project Green, involve pruning trees, removing dead trunks, construction waste and overgrown vegetation, and demolishing unauthorised structures. Ministers Alison Zerafa Civelli and Miriam Dalli visited the site.

item.title: St Julian's residents oppose plans for nine-floor hotel with rooftop bar
item.description: Residents in Triq il-Mensija are collecting signatures against an application to demolish the former Magister Academy school and build a nine-storey Class 3B hotel with 34 aparthotel units and a rooftop bar. Objectors say the height and the bar are incompatible with the North Harbours Local Plan and would extend Paceville into a residential street. Representations can be filed until 27 November.

item.title: Arnold Cassola to sue Neville Gafa for libel
item.description: Momentum chairman Arnold Cassola has filed a court application to sue Neville Gafa for defamation over claims made in an F Living interview broadcast on 7 October. Gafa called Cassola a hypocrite and alleged that a young girl was injured by negligence at a block of apartments he developed. Cassola said the claims were untrue and caused him reputational damage.

item.title: Temu levy impact on Maltese shoppers to be debated in European Parliament
item.description: A petition on the impact of the Temu levy on Maltese shoppers will be discussed by the European Parliament's Petitions Committee in January 2027. Maltese MEP and Vice-Coordinator Peter Agius announced his support for the petition, which calls for scrutiny of the import charges on low-cost online orders and their effect on local consumers and businesses.

item.title: President visits Maltese patients undergoing treatment in the UK
item.description: President Myriam Spiteri Debono departed for a three-day official visit to the United Kingdom, where she will meet Maltese patients receiving treatment at Great Ormond Street Hospital and the Royal Marsden Hospital, along with their families. Her itinerary also includes the Franciscan Sisters of the Heart of Jesus and Puttinu Cares apartments in Sutton, and an event at the Malta Tourism Authority's World Travel Market gathering in London.

item.title: Registered unemployed rose by 271 persons in a year
item.description: The number of people registered for work in Malta rose to 1,357 in September 2026, an increase of 271 on the same month a year earlier and roughly 25% above the annual base. Jobsplus data showed the largest rise among people aged 30 to 44, with 847 of those registered male and 510 female. Clerical roles accounted for 398 registrations, the largest category.

item.title: 64 families approved for fostering but have no children under their care
item.description: Parliamentary answers showed 224 families across Malta and Gozo are approved to provide foster care, but only 160 currently have children in their care. Social Policy Minister Michael Falzon said foster carers receive a €130 weekly allowance per child, and that recent budget measures phase down the allowance over four years or until a child turns 21 for families who go on to adopt.

item.title: Prison chief elected to international corrections board
item.description: Chris Siegersma, CEO of the Correctional Services Agency, was elected to the board of the International Corrections and Prisons Association at its annual conference in Belfast, the only European member among seven new appointees. Maltese NGO RISe Foundation also won a Community Corrections Award for its social reintegration programme, which works with inmates serving the last 12 to 15 months of their sentences.

item.title: Ten takeaways from Repubblika's proposals to reform the jury system
item.description: Malta Today summarised the main points of the Repubblika party's proposals on reforming the jury system, which have been at the centre of debate since three jury trials ended in acquittals within two months. The party has called for an independent review of the entire justice system, while the Attorney General's office has said the measures in the Scicluna case are best left before the courts.

item.title: eCabs expands into a second Croatian city with a third launch on the way
item.description: St Julian's-based eCabs Technologies said Taxi Barok in Varaždin has migrated onto its platform, following a launch with Taxi Fiume in Rijeka last August. item.title: Promotional Budget stickers removed from Valletta entrance
item.description: Giant stickers promoting the 2027 Budget were removed from Valletta's entrance just over a week after Finance Minister Clyde Caruana delivered his speech. Valletta Cultural Agency chairman Jason Micallef, who had criticised the stickers when they were placed hours after the Budget speech, said it was unacceptable for authorities to allow such clutter in a World Heritage city.

item.title: Attorney General seeks maximum sentence for Scicluna as prosecution defends prosecutors' record
item.description: The Attorney General's office said it has confidence in the professionalism and commitment of its prosecutors as criticism grows over two high-profile murder trials it has lost in two months. A jury cleared Lorin Scicluna of the racially motivated killing of Lassana Cisse on Sunday, shortly after Yorgen Fenech was acquitted over the murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia. On Wednesday the prosecution asked the court for the maximum sentence on Scicluna's two remaining convictions, grievous bodily harm against May Malimi in a 2019 hit-and-run and driving without number plates, while his defence argued the maximum was being sought to appease public opinion and should not be worsened by the public outcry over the acquittal. He is due to be sentenced on Thursday. Nationalist MP Mark Anthony Sammut called the three jury losses in two months unprecedented and accused Attorney General Victoria Buttigieg of having weakened the office.

He is due to be sentenced on Thursday. Nationalist MP Mark Anthony Sammut called the three jury losses in two months unprecedented and accused Attorney General Victoria Buttigieg of having weakened the office.

item.title: Public cannabis smoking to carry on-the-spot €235 fine
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield announced that tourists caught smoking cannabis in public will face an on-the-spot fine of €235, once the legal notice enters into force. The penalty will be added to the on-the-spot fines regime for non-habitual residents, which already covers offences such as littering, indecent dress outside bathing areas and urinating in the street. Bedingfield said police caught 42 people smoking cannabis in public between January and September 2026 and that residents frequently complain about public smoking on their streets. Maltese residents caught smoking in public will continue to face the applicable legal proceedings.

item.title: Enemalta issues almost €11m in tenders to reinforce Gozo's electricity network
item.description: Enemalta has issued two tenders worth almost €11 million for the supply and installation of new cables in Gozo. The larger, roughly €7 million contract covers trenching and the laying of new 33kV underground cables linking the 132kV distribution centre to the distribution centres in Xewkija and Qala and to the new Kerċem distribution centre. A second tender, valued at about €4 million, covers the supply and delivery of 33kV underground cables for the reinforcement programme. The projects cover electricity provision in Għajnsielem, Xewkija and the Xewkija-Victoria area.

item.title: 20-year-old granted bail in St Paul's Bay drug case
item.description: A 20-year-old man has been granted bail after pleading not guilty to charges of possessing cannabis and cocaine while breaching bail conditions. He is among the five people arrested during the drug trafficking raid in St Paul's Bay. The defence argued the quantities involved were very small. Magistrate Astrid May Grima granted bail against a €1,000 deposit and a €10,000 personal guarantee, with the accused ordered to sign the bail book three times a week and observe a curfew. The court also ordered a ban on publication of his name while investigations continue.

item.title: Ombudsman: leaving a phone number does not justify blocking garages
item.description: Ombudsman Joseph Zammit McKeon found that Transport Malta had incorrectly interpreted the law and told the authority to stop allowing drivers to park illegally in front of garages simply because they leave a telephone number on display. He also advised Transport Malta to coordinate with police and LESA officials when vehicles are parked unlawfully in front of a garage. The findings follow a complaint from a resident whose garage in Triq l-Imsida was repeatedly blocked by customers of a nearby business. Blocking a garage carries a €104.82 fine.

item.title: Freeport worker granted bail over alleged threats against his wife
item.description: A 51-year-old man employed at Freeport was granted bail after pleading not guilty to charges connected with alleged threats against his wife, said to have been made between 26 October and 3 November. After the victim filed a domestic violence report, authorities classified the case as high risk. The prosecution did not object to bail, with the inspector telling the court that family-related problems were at the heart of the case and that a protection order would suffice. The accused was granted bail against a €2,000 deposit and a €10,000 personal guarantee, ordered to stay away from Żejtun and placed under a protection order in favour of his wife.
